newsitem.title: USA: Chernomyrdin sees U.S.-Russia summit in late March.
newsitem.headline: Chernomyrdin sees U.S.-Russia summit in late March.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Thursday the summit between Russian President Boris Yeltsin and U.S. President Bill Clinton was being planned for the latter half of March.

Yeltsin's poor health had raised questions about when the long-planned summit would take place. Chernomyrdin, in Washington for a meeting of a U.S.-Russian liaison group, told reporters: "It is our job to prepare the summit of our presidents, the meeting that will take place in March, in the second half of the month."

Speaking in Russian, Chernomyrdin said the Yeltsin-Clinton summit would be "a very important meeting." He talked with reporters on a Washington street after a meeting with World Bank president James Wolfensohn.

It has not been announced where the summit would be held. It is Yeltsin's turn to visit the United States in the rotating summit plan, but there has been speculation it might be shifted to Europe to conserve Yeltsin's strength and the White House has said Clinton would be flexible on that issue.

The Russian prime minister arrived on Wednesday for talks with Vice President Al Gore during meetings of a Cabinet-level U.S.-Russian liaison group they head. He was to see Gore later Thursday and was expected to meet Clinton on Friday.

Chernomyrdin said European security would also be a focus of his talks with the Americans. Chernomyrdin has said he would warn Clinton that rapid expansion of NATO into central Europe could undermine Yeltsin's government.
